reason: The cited evidence supports the mechanical instability and spallation of oxide films during high-temperature wear (E1, E2), but provides no evidence for galvanic coupling, localized pitting at phase boundaries, or a synergistic wear-corrosion feedback loop. The key premises regarding corrosion mechanisms are entirely unsupported.
premises: Friction-induced oxide films on HEAs are mechanically unstable and prone to spallation under high-temperature wear.
Spallation of the oxide film exposes the underlying alloy, accelerating material loss.
Exposed phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs with differing electrochemical potentials promote galvanic coupling.
Galvanic coupling at phase boundaries accelerates localized pitting corrosion.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion create a synergistic feedback loop that intensifies degradation beyond additive effects.
